new_statements.quote: In the introduction Attobrah writes that, "Intonation or accent does not change the meaning of a word. The accent however is usually on the second syllable." It's not clear how this might interact with the long vowels.
new_statements.citation: Annis, William S. 2014. "Afrihili: An African Interlanguage." FL-00001F-00, Fiat Lingua, 1 April 2014, p. 4 (section 'The Language'), quoting the introduction of Attobrah, K. A. Kumi. 1973. Ni Afrihili Oluga: The African Continental Language (2nd ed.). Akrokerri: Afrihili Centre / Pyka Press.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (21 pp., the PDF's metadata OK; front matter reads 'Title: Afrihili: An African Interlanguage / Author: William S. Annis / FL Date: 04-01-2014 / FL Number: FL-00001F-00', CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, Fiat Lingua / Language Creation Society). The PDF text layer is a +3 character-shifted font encoding (extracted text gives '7KH /DQJXDJH' for 'The Language'); the saved and the tesseract scanned both undo it, and I additionally rendered PDF p. 5 (printed page 4) to PNG and read it visually. The passage is there verbatim, section 'The Language', 4th paragraph, printed p. 4 = PDF p. 5: 'In the introduction Attobrah writes that, "Intonation or accent does not change the meaning of a word. The accent ho…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language designer states that accent is not distinctive and 'usually' falls on the second syllable of the word (counted from the left); no tone. Annis notes the interaction with (orthographically doubled) long vowels is unspecified. The English Wikipedia claim 'Stress is on the second-last vowel' is a 2011 unsourced editorial rewrite of this same sentence, so the earlier scan's penult reading rests on no primary wording.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'usually'; no exceptions or examples given. Contradiction to flag: en.wikipedia (since 2011) says 'second-last vowel' (penult), whereas Attobrah's own words as quoted by Annis, the 2006-2010 Wikipedia text, and the German and French Wikipedia articles all say 'second syllable'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('the meaning of a word'); a designed rule for a constructed language, not an observed one; no instrumental or speaker data exist.
new_statements.identity_note: Afrihili is a constructed international auxiliary language (Glottolog family 'Artificial Language', arti1236; ISO 639-3 afh), designed by K. A. Kumi Attobrah of Akrokerri, Ghana; no dialects or speaker community. The 2026-09-12 catalog reading (confirmed by the second reader) already ruled it not a distinct language under our rule excluding constructed languages, which is why proposed for the catalogis false despite a quotable statement.

sources.quote: In the introduction Attobrah writes that, "Intonation or accent does not change the meaning of a word. The accent however is usually on the second syllable." It's not clear how this might interact with the long vowels.
sources.locator: Annis 2014, p. 4 = PDF p. 5, section 'The Language', 4th paragraph; Annis fn. 4 states the 1973 edition is used; the quoted sentences are from Attobrah's introduction (book has no page numbers)
sources.note: Section 'The Language', p. 4 (PDF p. 5): quotes the introduction of Attobrah's 1973 edition verbatim: 'Intonation or accent does not change the meaning of a word. The accent however is usually on the second syllable.' and adds 'It's not clear how this might interact with the long vowels.' Footnote 4 says all information is from the 1973 edition; the reference list (p. 20) gives Attobrah, Kumi. 1972. Ni Afrihili Oluga. Pyka Press.

sources.note: 'There is no tone. Stress is on the second-last vowel.' Unsourced. Revision history (oldid_*.wiki files) shows the 2006-2010 text read 'Intonation or accent does not change the meaning of a word. The accent however is usually on the second syllable.' (Attobrah's own wording); the 'second-last vowel' sentence was introduced by editor Kwamikagami in rev 431394877 (2011-05-28) with no edit summary or source.
